newsitem.title: USA: COOL TEMPS, BUT NO HARM TO BRAZIL COFFEE - CROPCAST.
newsitem.headline: COOL TEMPS, BUT NO HARM TO BRAZIL COFFEE - CROPCAST.

text.p: Temperatures turned cooler this past weekend in Brazil, but the country's coffee crop escaped unscathed, U.S.-based forecaster Cropcast said on Monday.

"Cold weekend temperatures did not harm the coffee crop," Cropcast said in its daily weather summary. "Although some widely scattered areas of light frost were reported across the far southern portions of the belt over the weekend, any damage that occurred to the coffee crop was negligible."
Cropcast said the coolest mornings were on Sunday and Monday, when lows dropped back into the 40s to low 50s F (mid-single digits to low teens C) across north-central portions of the coffee belt.

In some locations across Parana and the far southern fringes of Sao Paulo low temperatures fell to the 33 to 39 F (1 to 4 C) range and there were some widely scattered occurences of light frost, Cropcast said.

In the short term, Cropcast said an area of high pressure will remain just off of the Brazilian coast through the middle of this week resulting in mostly dry and cool conditions. Low temperatures will range from the upper 30s F (4 to 5 C) across the far south to the low 50s F (11 to 12 C) across the northwest.
In its extended six-to-ten-day outlook, Cropcast said temperatures are expected to moderate to above normal levels, with no damaging cold forecast.
"There are no threats of frost foreseen through the middle of next week, and the harvest should make good progress due to the lack of significant rainfall," Cropcast said.
